abstract: Cerebral ischemia disrupts energy-dependent ion transport and causes acute brain injury. The synchronization modulation electric field (SMEF) platform was developed to support Na+/K+-ATPase function under conditions of limited ATP availability and has shown protective effects in renal ischemia models. We investigated whether cerebral cortical application of third-generation SMEF attenuates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats. Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent sham surgery or transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) for 120 min, with or without SMEF treatment during ischemia. At 24 h after reperfusion, we assessed body-weight change, neurological deficits, open-field locomotor activity, cerebral infarct volume using 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining, hemispheric swelling, and cortical and striatal histopathology. Western blot analysis was performed to measure Na+/K+-ATPase 1, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and nuclear factor kappa B (NF-{kappa}B) p65 protein abundance. Compared with untreated MCAO rats, SMEF-treated rats exhibited significantly less body-weight loss, lower neurological deficit scores, greater total distance traveled, smaller edema-corrected infarct volumes and percentages, and lower cortical and striatal injury scores. SMEF also shifted Na+/K+-ATPase 1, GFAP, and NF-{kappa}B p65 protein abundance toward sham levels. These findings support an acute protective effect of SMEF following transient MCAO. Further studies should assess Na+/K+-ATPase activity and longer-term functional, histological, and molecular outcomes.
